title: Contract Renewal: Phased Billing, Annual Reconciliation & Uplift Framework
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: This ticket creates a repeatable framework for enterprise contract renewals that combines a phased billing option (to smooth invoice impact across a transition quarter), an annual reconciliation cadence (consumption-based audit and adjustment), and a clear set of uplift rules for expansion and multi-year commitments. The goal is to reduce sticker shock at renewal, enable predictable ARR recognition for sales, and automate the reconciliation path so engineering and billing teams have fewer manual interventions.

What we propose: 
1) Phased Billing Option (optional add-on):
   - Mechanics: When a customer converts from a trial or self-serve plan to a committed enterprise contract mid-quarter, offer a 3-month phased billing schedule where the commitment is billed monthly at a prorated committed rate. Phased billing transitions to the normal annual or monthly invoice at the start of the following billing cycle.
   - Use cases: customers who sign late in a quarter; customers with procurement cycles that do not align to calendar year.
   - Accounting note: Recognize committed ARR pro rata. Finance has sign-off on revenue recognition guidance in Confluence (link below).

2) Annual Reconciliation (consumption true-up):
   - Mechanics: At the end of each 12-month commitment, perform a consumption reconciliation comparing committed units (tokens/embedding-units/dedicated GPU-days) against actual usage. Overages above the committed quantity are billed as a single reconciliation invoice with the agreed uplift tiers. Under-usage credits are applied to the customer account and can be rolled forward per contract.
   - Audit & transparency: Provide customers with a reconciliation report (CSV + dashboard permalink) that shows month-by-month usage, cache hit ratios, and any autoscaling events that impacted consumption. Legal requires audit rights language; finance provided standard wording (Confluence link).

3) Uplift & Multi-year Discount Rules:
   - Graduated uplift tiers for reconciliation (example): 0-10% over commit = 1.0x unit rate; 10-40% = 1.15x; 40-100% = 1.35x; >100% = 1.6x (cap negotiated for enterprise). Rationale: encourage accurate commiting, limit billing surprises, align incentives for customers to buy appropriate capacity.
   - Multi-year discounts: Provide a step-down discount schedule tied to term length and minimum ARR. For example: 12 mo = 0% baseline; 24 mo = 7% off list; 36 mo = 12% off list. Discounts apply to committed baseline only and do not apply to reconciliation overages.
   - Ramp credits: For customers expecting growth, offer a 6-month ramp credit equal to X% of committed baseline to reduce early churn risk. Ramp credits are applied as invoice credits and tracked in the billing system.

Trade-offs & decisions: 
- Simplicity vs precision: Graduated uplift tiers simplify billing math but may overcharge for transient spikes; we trade off revenue precision for operational simplicity.
- Audit burden: Providing detailed reconciliation reports increases trust but requires engineering support to surface KV cache and autoscaling metadata. ENG-6123 is dependency to implement export hooks.
- Discount aggressiveness: Higher multi-year discounts improve retention (NRR) but reduce short-term ARR. Experiment will quantify elasticity.

Integration and automation: 
- Billing system: Integrate with Zuora (primary) and Stripe (secondary for smaller customers). Implement a reconciliation job that pulls usage from usage-warehouse, applies uplift rules and creates reconciliation invoice draft for finance review.
- Reporting: Add reconciliation dashboard in Metabase with filters by customer, contract, period and uplift-impacted revenue. Link to supporting spreadsheet: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/FIN/pages/RENEWAL-RECONCILE (placeholder).

Success metrics: 
- Primary: Reduce renewal churn attributable to billing surprises by 25% in cohort by Q4 2025.
- Secondary: Reduce manual reconciliation labor (finance tickets) by 60% within first 6 months of rollout. Increase multi-year commitments share of new ARR to 30% for enterprise deals.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Product: UI copy and contract language drafted and approved; Sales has scripts and playbook; RD for optional phased billing toggle in contract UI implemented.
- Engineering: Automated reconciliation pipeline that produces draft invoices and reconciliation report (ENG-6123 complete).
- Finance/Legal: Approval on revenue recognition treatment and audit clauses; billing templates updated.
- Observability: Reconciliation dashboard live in Metabase with sample dataset for 3 pilot customers.

Open questions: 
- Should uplift tiers be negotiated on a per-account basis for top-tier customers? (finance prefers template, sales wants flexibility).
- How do we handle committed GPU-days vs token-based commitments for hybrid workloads? Need input from Applied ML.
- Thresholds for under-usage credits (floor to avoid gaming).

References & artifacts: 
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/CONTRACT-RENEWAL-FRAMEWORK (draft)
- Finance spreadsheet (model): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/renewal-model (placeholder)
- Example clause (legal): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEGAL/pages/AUDIT-CONSUMPTION-CLAUSE (placeholder)
- Pilot cohort list (internal): Drive: /Shared/renewals/pilot-2025.csv

Next steps: 
- 2025-02-18: Finance review of uplift tiers and invoice flows (owner: Miguel Santos).
- 2025-02-28: Engineering kickoff to spec export hooks and reconciliation job (owner: ENG-6123).
- 2025-03-06: Legal finalize audit & under-usage language.
- 2025-03-15: Finalize pilot contracts for two strategic customers, enable phased billing toggle, and run first reconciliation mock.

Notes for sales: Include FAQ about phased billing and ramp credits in deal desk materials. Use the new playbook to reduce negotiation cycles on invoice timing.
